cards.name: Brick Wall
cards.summary: Texture effect that makes the picture look painted onto a brick wall: the image keeps its colours but is broken into courses of bricks separated by grout lines, each brick shaded in relief from the light direction, with Roughness pitting the brick surface. Brick Width / Height and Grout Width set the scale of the wall.
use_for: mural / street-art look where a photo or logo should read as painted on brickwork (event backdrop, poster)
cafe, pub or urban-brand menu and signage mock-ups
textured background plate behind headline type
avoid: faces and small detail: grout lines cut straight through features; keep bricks large or apply it only to a background bitmap
an editable, recolourable brick pattern: use a pattern fill on a vector shape instead of a bitmap texture
the scripted path works on bitmaps only (Shape.Bitmap): run Object/Convert to Bitmap on vector art first

scripts: this effect's command string has not been apply-tested (format proven on 6 other effects) and the bool spelling for MaintainAspectRatio (1/0) is unproven; a before/after pixel diff proves nothing because a wrong key still applies the effect at the dialog's values: apply two different values and compare those

params.name: Roughness
params.does: how pitted and uneven the brick surface is (0 = smooth bricks)

params.name: BrickWidth
params.does: width of each brick (1-1000; the harvest records no unit)

params.name: BrickHeight
params.does: height of each brick (1-1000)

params.name: MaintainAspectRatio
params.does: links brick width and height so changing one scales the other

params.name: GroutWidth
params.does: thickness of the mortar lines between bricks

params.name: LightDirection
params.does: angle in degrees (0-360, 5-degree steps) the light comes from, which sets which brick edges are lit and which are shadowed
params.typical: 315 (default; the harvest does not record which screen direction an angle points to)

pairs_with: Object/Convert to Bitmap (gives vector art a bitmap for the scripted path)
Effects/Adjust colour effects before it to push the mural colours
a soft vignette or transparency on the edges so the wall fades into the layout

cards.name: Bubbles
cards.summary: Covers the image with a layer of round foam / soap bubbles, each lit as a small shiny sphere from the light direction: Coverage sets how much of the picture is buried under bubbles and Diameter their size; with Refraction on, each bubble bends the image behind it like a small lens. How the bubbles are drawn is from general knowledge of the effect, not tested in this harvest.
use_for: playful foam / soap look for a detergent, bath-product or kids' party poster
fizzy-drink or underwater themed background plates
a decorative bubble overlay on a background photo behind type
avoid: images where faces or text must stay readable: high Coverage buries them; keep Coverage low or apply it to a background bitmap only
art-directed bubbles at chosen positions and sizes: draw vector circles with fountain fills and transparency instead
the scripted path works on bitmaps only (Shape.Bitmap): run Object/Convert to Bitmap on vector art first

params.name: Refraction

cards.name: Canvas
cards.summary: Lays a canvas-cloth texture map over the image and embosses it, so the picture reads as printed or painted on woven canvas. The texture is a canvas image picked in the dialog (CurrentCanvasImage), tiled in rows or columns or stretched to fit; Transparency sets how the canvas map blends with the picture and Emboss how deep the weave's relief is.
use_for: fine-art / gallery-print look for a portrait, painting reproduction or wedding album page
canvas-print product mock-ups and art-sale posters
adding a subtle woven tooth to a flat digital image
avoid: small text or hairlines in the bitmap: the weave breaks them up; keep type as vectors above the bitmap
choosing a specific canvas texture from a script: CurrentCanvasImage has no harvested values, so a script gets whatever the dialog last used; pick it in the dialog
the scripted path works on bitmaps only (Shape.Bitmap): run Object/Convert to Bitmap on vector art first
scripts: command string not apply-tested (format proven on 6 other effects)

scripts: every command form tried (Transparency 100 and 50, with and without the offsets, Mode as a name or an index) changed no pixel without a fault; the canvas texture is probably dialog state (CurrentCanvasImage), so apply it from the dialog

params.name: Transparency
params.does: how the canvas texture map blends with the image (0-100, default 100); the harvest does not record which end shows the most canvas, so judge it in the preview
params.typical: default 100, lower to change the canvas tint

params.name: Emboss
params.does: depth of the weave's relief shading (0-200)

params.name: XOffset
params.does: shifts the canvas texture horizontally (-100 to 100)

params.name: YOffset
params.does: shifts the canvas texture vertically (-100 to 100)

params.name: Mode
params.does: how the canvas image covers the bitmap: tiled in Rows, tiled in Columns, or Stretch (Stretch to fit) as one image

params.name: TileOffset
params.does: offset between successive tile rows / columns (0-100), staggering the repeats so seams line up less

params.name: CurrentCanvasImage
params.does: which canvas texture image is used (list in the dialog; no values harvested)

pairs_with: a painterly effect before it (Art Strokes) for a full oil-on-canvas look
Object/Convert to Bitmap (bitmap needed for the scripted path)

cards.name: Cobblestone
cards.summary: Rebuilds the image as a cobblestone pavement: the picture is cut into irregular rounded stones separated by grout channels, each stone shaded in relief from the light direction while keeping the image's colours. Size sets the stones, Grout width the gaps, Roughness the pitted surface; Warp is a checkbox the harvest does not describe. The stone layout is random: a live audit applied the same command twice and got different pixels.
use_for: old-town / heritage street feel for travel, food-walk or festival posters
rustic stone-mosaic treatment of a landscape or texture photo
a textured stone background plate behind type
avoid: work that must re-render identically (variants, a series, before/after): the stone pattern changes on every application (audit verdict 'nondeterministic'); render once and keep the bitmap
faces and fine detail: grout channels slice through them; use it on backgrounds
scripted values beyond the dialog ranges (Roughness 0-100, Size and Grout width 1-100, Direction 0-360): the audit's Roughness=410 was applied without error and what it does is unknown
the scripted path works on bitmaps only (Shape.Bitmap): run Object/Convert to Bitmap on vector art first

params.name: Direction

params.name: Warp

cards.name: Etching
cards.summary: Turns the image into an etched metal plate: the picture's colours are replaced by one surface colour (set in the dialog) and its edges and tones become fine engraved grooves and raised areas lit from the light direction, like a copper or brass etching. Detail sets how much fine line work survives, Depth how deep the relief reads.
use_for: metal plaque / commemorative-plate look for an award, certificate or anniversary graphic
engraved-metal treatment of a portrait or emblem for a premium label
a monochrome relief texture for a background
avoid: photos whose colour matters: the output is one surface colour
soft, low-contrast images: there is little edge detail to etch; raise contrast (Effects/Adjust/Brightness/Contrast/Intensity) or Detail first
a softer carved-stone look: use Effects/Texture/Relief Sculpture; a plain grey emboss: Effects/3D Effects/Emboss
setting the surface colour from a script: Surface Color (SurfaceColorItem) is not in the command template

cards.name: Screen Door
cards.summary: Makes the image look as if seen through a fine mesh screen such as a fly-screen door: a regular grid of thin wires over a softened picture. By their names Mesh Density sets how fine the grid is, Softness how soft the image behind looks and Brightness the overall lightness; BackgroundColor switches between a Black and White and a Color rendering, but which part it affects is not recorded. These readings come from the names only, not from a test.
use_for: a 'seen through the screen' or voyeur-window mood for a film, drama or thriller poster
a fine mesh / grid texture over a background photo behind type
retro LED-screen or mesh-banner feel
avoid: anything that needs sharp detail: the mesh and softening obscure it
a printed halftone or screen-print dot look: use Effects/Color Transform/Halftone instead
the scripted path works on bitmaps only (Shape.Bitmap): run Object/Convert to Bitmap on vector art first
scripts: command string not apply-tested (format proven on 6 other effects)

params.name: BackgroundColor
params.does: Black and White or Color rendering (default Black and White); exactly which part it colours is not recorded
params.typical: Black and White (default) or Color; try both in the preview

params.name: Density
params.does: Mesh Density: how fine the mesh grid is (1-60)

params.name: Softness
params.does: how soft the image seen through the mesh looks (1-100)

params.name: Brightness
params.does: overall lightness of the result (1-100)

pairs_with: Object/Convert to Bitmap (bitmap needed for the scripted path)
a dark vignette for a moody poster
bold vector type above the bitmap so the mesh does not cut it
cards.scripting: shape.Bitmap.ApplyBitmapEffect("PGD Screen Door", "ScreenDoorEffect BackgroundColor=Color,Density=20,Softness=60,Brightness=100")  // shape must be a bitmap; template 'ScreenDoorEffect BackgroundColor=<enum>,Density=<number>,Softness=<number>,Brightness=<number>'; enum values 'Black and White' / 'Color' (the space-containing value may need quoting, unproven); string not apply-tested; a misspelt key is not rejected (this batch's Elephant Skin / Cobblestone audits: 'NoSuchKey...' still applied the effect at the dialog's values), so prove a key by applying two values, not by a before/after diff. Menu route (dialog): Application.FrameWork.Automation.InvokeItem("f507cc7f-cd56-4ba9-9e99-797d3e21cfe6")
cards.non_destructive: yes from the Effects menu: CorelDRAW 2024 keeps it in the object's effect stack (ApplyOrDeleteEffect:ScreenDoorEffect); the scripted path was not checked
cards.cost: light to moderate: a softening pass plus a mesh overlay (estimate, not timed)

review.changes: scripting: added that a misspelt key is silently ignored (audit BADKEY), so test keys with two values; cost marked as not timed; BackgroundColor typical: dropped 'Color keeps the photo's colours', which contradicted 'which part it colours is not recorded'; avoid: named the harvested Effects/Color Transform/Halftone

verified.note: Seen through a fine mesh: at 6x zoom a regular grid of thin dark wires covers the softened picture, and the frame is darker overall (mean 93 vs 133).
